title: Tinkerbench compact log — Harper
content:
Purpose:
Quick personal tracker for micro-experiments with small model variants and batching/cache tweaks. Use for jotting per-run numbers (p50/p95 latency, token throughput, rough cost), quick hypotheses, and immediate follow-ups. Not canonical — working notes.

How I use this sheet:
- One row per run (not per minute).
- Short tag in 'run_id' to map back to saved logs.
- Keep measurements from same warmup pattern (10 warmup requests then measure 30 requests).
- Use cost_est as back-of-envelope using 0.00012 $/k token for hosted baseline (placeholder).

Columns: date | run_id | model | q (quant) | batch | prefix_cache | p50_ms | p95_ms | tokens_total | approx_cost_usd | notes

Data (most recent first):
2026-02-27 | tb-026 | redwood-v1-small | q4_0 | 8 | kv-on | 42 | 120 | 12,400 | 0.15 | baseline for small; p95 jump on long sequences, likely GC during batch flush
2026-02-25 | tb-025 | redwood-v1-small | q4_0 | 16 | kv-on | 55 | 190 | 18,200 | 0.22 | batch 16 increases p95 significantly -- investigate scheduling spikes on node 3
2026-02-22 | tb-024 | redwood-v1-small | q4_0 | 8 | kv-off | 68 | 210 | 11,900 | 0.14 | no cache = p50 +60% -> cache still worth it for prefix-heavy traffic
2026-01-12 | tb-011 | redwood-v1-base | q8_1 | 4 | kv-on | 78 | 250 | 9,500 | 0.11 | base model higher tail latency; try reduced batch or kernel fallback
2025-12-03 | tb-003 | tiny-distil | q4_0 | 32 | kv-on | 21 | 48 | 25,000 | 0.30 | good throughput for short prompts; watch CPU on preproc thread

Quick observations (scratch):
- kv-on wins for repeated prefixes (p50 down ~30%) but increases memory pressure; monitor OOM metrics when batch > 12.
- p95 spikes often coincide with GC logs around 00:00 UTC in this env (older nodes). Add a cron schedule to rotate logs off-peak.
- q8_1 improves p50 vs q4_0 for base model but cost & tail tradeoffs ambiguous. Need token-level quality check.

Immediate next actions (short TODO):
- [ ] Re-run tb-025 with node 3 isolated to confirm scheduling impact (assign to Ravi).
- [ ] Add lightweight per-request trace id to correlate p95 with GC logs (Maya to prototype).
- [ ] Sweep kernel flags: turn on aten-fused-attn for base model and compare (measuring both p50/p95).
- [ ] Produce small prompt set (20 prompts) and run quality check for q8_1 vs q4_0 (manual diff).

Open questions / hypotheses:
- Are p95 spikes primarily scheduling or memory reclamation? hypothesis: memory reclaim (GC) + batching alignment -> causes tails.
- Does larger batch always harm tail for small models? suspect threshold around 12-16 where queueing builds up.

Notes to self:
- Keep run IDs consistent: tb-XXX; prefix with two letters to indicate bench type (tb = tinkerbench).
- When copying into perf repo, include the raw metrics JSON (s3://perf-archive/tb/YYYYMM).

Past related quick links:
- perf dashboard (internal): https://console.redwood.ai/perf/dashboards/tinkerbench
- node logs (s3): s3://redwood-ops/node-logs/2026-02/

One-line summary for README:
"Tinkerbench compact — small personal table to capture run numbers, quick triage notes, and immediate follow-ups for micro-bench experiments (batching/cache/quantization)."

End of sheet.
